title: Thundering Herd Simulation Playbook
content:
Goal:
Run a set of quick, reproducible synthetic experiments to understand system behavior during short, high-intensity 'thundering herd' spikes. Focus areas: connection churn effects, cold-KV priming penalty, batch coalescing window behavior, and graceful shedding / retry patterns. This is a lightweight playbook (notes + runnable params) so we can iterate fast and share with SRE and product when we have clear signals.

Setup / environment:
- Cluster: dev-gpu-pool-4 (4xA100-same-gen), model: distil-rlm-v2 quantized (int8), config: default kernel selection.
- Runtime: serving-runtime@main (PR 789 branch for coalescing changes).
- Load generator: custom k6 wrapper (local harness) and a small goroutine-based TCP client for connection storm variants.
- KV cache toggles: off / warm / cold. Use header X-KV-Primed: true to simulate warm cache route.
- Traffic shape: short pulses, 10s window, 500–2k qps peak, Poisson vs synchronized fanout.
- Instrumentation: token-level trace, connection histograms, batch size distributions, per-request path (cache-miss / hit).

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Pattern A: Synchronized fanout (all clients send at t=0 in 10s window) — baseline for worst-case connection storm.
- Pattern B: Randomized Poisson spike same mean QPS — compare jitter effects.
- Pattern C: Synchronized but with TCP preconnect pool + keepalive (client-side) — test connection re-use mitigation.
- Pattern D: Same as A but with batch-coalescing enabled (coalescing window 5ms / 10ms / 20ms).
- Pattern E: Same as A but with KV primed on 80% of requests.
- Pattern F: Add preemptive-backoff server flag (experimental) to see shedding behavior.

Representative raw run excerpts (timestamps are local test wall clock):

--- Run A.1 (Baseline sync fanout, cold cache) ---
params: 1200 clients, each sends 1 req at t=0 within 10s window, payload 512 tokens, no preconnect
observed: peak qps ~1180, concurrency spike ~340
errors: 0.8% 503 throttles during 2s window
latency: p50=52ms, p95=160ms, p99=540ms, p999=1720ms
batches: mean batch size=1.7, heavy right tail (many singletons)
notes: connection ramp and gating seems to cause serialization on accept path. KV misses amplified p99.

--- Run B.2 (Poisson spike, cold cache) ---
params: poisson arrivals, mean qps ~1200, same payload
observed: peak qps ~1150, concurrency steady ~210
errors: 0.2% 502 transient timeouts
latency: p50=48ms, p95=120ms, p99=320ms, p999=980ms
batches: mean batch size=2.9, smoother tail
notes: jitter distributed load; kernel selection better utilized. Much lower tail latency vs A.1.

--- Run C.1 (Synchronized + TCP preconnect pool, cold cache) ---
params: same as A.1 but client preconnect pool keeps 8 connections open each
observed: peak qps ~1220, concurrency ~260
errors: 0.25% 502 on a short spike only
latency: p50=46ms, p95=110ms, p99=290ms, p999=940ms
batches: mean batch size=3.2
notes: preconnect removed accept-path contention; tail improved significantly. Suggest default client SDK preconnect or connection-reuse guidance.

--- Run D.3 (Synchronized + coalescing window 10ms) ---
params: coalescing window server-side = 10ms, same sync fanout
observed: peak qps ~1250, concurrency ~220
errors: 0.15% 502 transient (retries handled)
latency: p50=54ms, p95=130ms, p99=270ms, p999=760ms
batches: mean batch size=6.8, heavy middle mass around 6-9
notes: coalescing raised mean batch size which amortized kernel overhead and reduced p99 vs A.1. Slight p50 increase due to small waiting window but acceptable given SLO.

--- Run E.1 (Synchronized + KV primed 80%) ---
params: same as A.1 but 80% requests have prefix in KV cache
observed: peak qps ~1180, concurrency ~200
errors: 0.12% 502
latency: p50=36ms, p95=90ms, p99=220ms, p999=660ms
batches: mean batch size=3.6
notes: KV priming had biggest single win on tail; p99 down ~60% vs cold baseline. Recomm: prefix caching/priming for predicted hot keys (client or warm cache API).

--- Run F.1 (Synchronized + preemptive-backoff) ---
params: server preemptive-backoff enabled (soft shed threshold at 250 concurrency)
observed: incoming qps peaked but server dropped ~1.1% of requests intentionally and replied with 429+Retry-After
errors: synthetic 429s, client retries handled with backoff
latency: p50=42ms, p95=95ms, p99=260ms
notes: graceful shedding kept overall tail under control and avoided long GC/queue stalls. However user-visible 429s need client-facing retry guidance and metrics to avoid UX regressions.

Quick observations / hypotheses:
- Accept/connection hot path is a major multiplier for synchronized spikes. Mitigation: client preconnect OR server-side accept sharding (probe ticket: INF-4432).
- Coalescing windows show clear tradeoff: small wait (5-20ms) reduces p99 dramatically by increasing batch size. We need a default of 10ms with dynamic backoff for low-latency tenants.
- KV priming is the highest leverage intervention for model-lookup heavy routes. Consider on-deploy warmup and a priming endpoint.
- Preemptive shedding keeps system stable but requires careful product communication (retry semantics).

Quick actionable checklist (for follow-up runs / PRs):
- [ ] Add client SDK docs snippet for preconnect and recommended pool sizes (8 by default).
- [ ] Run A/B tests with coalescing default 10ms vs 0ms across two dev clusters for longer runs (1 hour) to observe steady-state costs.
- [ ] Add per-tenant coalescing config flag (dev) and a dashboard to visualize batch-size vs latency.
- [ ] Implement a KV priming utility (script) that walks a common prompt set; measure warmup time to 95% hit rate.
- [ ] Wire an alert on 'accept queue depth > 100ms' to catch accept-path contention early.

Notes to self / quick heuristics for next time:
- When p999 > 3x p99, suspect head-of-line accept or GC spike, not model kernel.
- Batch-size target: 4-8 tokens per GPU is sweet spot for our distil-rlm-v2 on these instances.
- Coalescing window 10ms seems a practical default; start small for UX-critical endpoints.

Raw artifacts / commands used (for reproducibility):
- k6 wrapper: ./tools/loadgen/k6-thunder --clients 1200 --pattern sync --duration 10s --payload 512 --out /tmp/runA1.json
- tcp preconnect harness: ./tools/tcpstorm --preconnect 8 --clients 1200 --payload 512 --out /tmp/runC1.json
- collect traces: /scripts/collect-traces.sh dev-gpu-pool-4 run-A1 /tmp/traces-A1.tar.gz

Next steps: formalize this into an infra experiment ticket (INF-4433) with proposed mitigations: client preconnect SDK patch, coalescing default, and short KV priming workflow. If SRE wants, we can run a 6-hour canary on dedicated capacity to estimate cost delta from coalescing vs no-coalescing.

Logs / ad-hoc notes: kept a few stack traces and flamegraphs in /tmp (point to linked artifacts in PR). Follow up with Maya for longer run capacity planning and Samir for SDK snippet review.

-- Owen
